- [LEXP.7.1a] **The arithmetic operators require numeric operands.** `+`, `-`,
  `*`, `/`, `//` and `%` take `Int` or `Float`. The compiler must refuse a
  `String` operand with `DS_VALIDATE_BAD_OPERAND_TYPE`, wherever the
  expression stands, a `const` right-hand side included ([LEXP.8.8]): there is
  no string `+`, between two literals or any other operands.
  Build strings with interpolation ([LGRA.2.9.6]), which is the one surface for
  it — a second spelling would be two paths that have to agree on every edge,
  the shape [RTIM.14.8] exists to prevent.

  Stated because the alternative is silent: an accepted `s.a + s.b` evaluates to
  an absent value, and an absent value in a predicate never fires ([LNUL.4.3]),
  so `where s.a + s.b == "xy"` is **false for every input including the one it
  was written for**. A compile error costs the author one edit and says where.
